question_text: A 24-year-old man, an information technology professional, gets himself tested for serum immunoglobulin M (IgM) levels because he wants to know more about his immunity. The physician discusses human immunity and its important components. He also tells him that most circulating IgM antibodies in the blood of normal persons are produced by a specific type of B cell, which is present mostly in the peritoneal cavity and in mucosal tissues. He also mentions that these cells are components of innate immunity. Which of the following types of B cells is the physician referring to?

He also mentions that these cells are components of innate immunity. Which of the following types of B cells is the physician referring to?
